## Sign Up

Switch to the **Sign up** tab and provide your name (or nickname), email, and
password (entered twice to confirm). The form is the same whether you use
Econumo at [app.econumo.com](https://app.econumo.com/register) or Econumo
Self-Hosted.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

**Econumo at app.econumo.com**
A new account starts with a 45-day free trial, and no payment card is required
to sign up. To keep using Econumo after the trial, make a one-time payment.
See [Econumo Editions](/docs/edition/) for details.

**Econumo Self-Hosted**
Administrators can disable open registration with the
`ECONUMO_ALLOW_REGISTRATION` environment variable and create users from the
[CLI](/docs/self-hosting/cli-commands/) instead.

---
## Sign In

To sign in, enter the email and password you provided during sign-up. If your
Econumo instance enables single sign-on, an **or continue with** divider below
the form offers **Google**, **Apple**, or a custom OpenID Connect provider,
alongside the password form.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

**Note**
Signing in through a provider for the first time creates a new, passwordless
account if your server allows registration. You can add a password afterwards
from **Settings → Personal settings → Change password**, or link the provider to an
account you already have from
[Sign-in methods](/docs/user-guide/user-profile/#sign-in-methods).

**Econumo Self-Hosted**
Administrators can turn password sign-in off entirely with the
`ECONUMO_PASSWORD_LOGIN` environment variable. On such an instance the sign-in
and sign-up screens show only the provider buttons — no email/password
fields, no **or continue with** divider, and no **Forgot password?** link —
and **Settings → Personal settings → Security** no longer offers **Change password** or
**Set a password**.

---
## Password Recovery

Click **Forgot password?** on the sign-in screen, enter your email, and press
**Send code**.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

If an account exists with the provided email, you will receive a security code.
Enter the code, choose a new password, and press **Reset password**:

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

**Note**
Resetting your password is a deliberate account reclaim, not just a password
change: it signs you out everywhere, revokes API tokens, and unlinks any
sign-in provider that vouches for a different email address than your own.
Your shared budgets and connections are left alone.

---
## Getting started

After your first sign-in, Econumo walks you through setup in a few short
steps. The bar at the top shows where you are (*"Getting started · 2 of 5"*);
tap a step to jump to it.

1. **Import** *(optional)* — **Bring in your history**: choose a CSV export
   from your bank or another app, and Econumo creates accounts, categories and
   transactions in one go (see [CSV Import](/docs/user-guide/csv-import-export/#importing-transactions-from-csv)).
   No file? Press **I don't have one**.
2. **Categories** — **What do you spend on?** Econumo suggests a starting list
   of expense and income categories. Remove what you don't need, rename them,
   change their icons, or add your own.
3. **Accounts** — **Where's your money right now?** Add your accounts with
   their current balances and currencies; no history is needed.
4. **Budget & plan** — **Plan this month**: enter rough planned amounts for
   your income and expenses. You can adjust them later.
5. **Connect** — **Connect your accounts** so transactions come in on their
   own: set up [Apple Wallet](/docs/user-guide/apple-wallet/) or
   [SimpleFIN](/docs/user-guide/simplefin/), or copy the [MCP address](/docs/user-guide/ai-assistants/) for an AI
   assistant such as Claude or ChatGPT.

When your browser can install Econumo, an extra step offers to add it to your
home screen (see
[Installing Econumo as an app](/docs/user-guide/#installing-econumo-as-an-app)).

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

Press **Complete setup** when you are done — you can do it from any step.
Everything the wizard sets up stays available in **Settings** afterwards.

---
## Finding your way around

Your accounts, grouped into folders, fill the sidebar on desktop and tablet and
the home screen on mobile; **Budget & Plan** above them opens your
[budget](/docs/user-guide/budgets/) and its
[Plan view](/docs/user-guide/plan/). Next to the Econumo logo at the top sit
two buttons: [Search](/docs/user-guide/search/) (also on **Ctrl+K** / **⌘K**)
and the [Inbox](/docs/user-guide/inbox/), whose badge counts what is waiting on
you. At the bottom, next to **Settings**, the chart icon opens
[Reports](/docs/user-guide/reports/) and the sync button refreshes your data
(and syncs [SimpleFIN](/docs/user-guide/simplefin/), if you use it).

Everything that is not day-to-day spending lives in **Settings**, in these
groups:

- **Billing** — **Manage subscription**, on econumo.com (not on self-hosted
  servers).
- **Finances** — [Accounts](/docs/user-guide/accounts/),
  [Shared access](/docs/user-guide/shared-access/), **Budgets & Plans**, and
  [Recurring transactions](/docs/user-guide/recurring-transactions/).
- **Classification** — [Categories, Tags, Payees](/docs/user-guide/classifications/)
  and [Currencies](/docs/user-guide/currencies/).
- **Data** — the ways to [import data](/docs/user-guide/import-data/):
  **Import & export** for
  [CSV import and export](/docs/user-guide/csv-import-export/),
  [Apple Wallet](/docs/user-guide/apple-wallet/),
  [SimpleFIN](/docs/user-guide/simplefin/),
  [Import rules](/docs/user-guide/import-rules/), and **Clear cache and
  reload**, which downloads all your data again.
- **Feedback** — **Send feedback**: tell us what you like, ask for a feature,
  or report a bug.

On desktop and tablet, open Settings from the bottom of the sidebar; on mobile,
from the bottom of the home screen. The card with your name at the top opens
your [Personal settings](/docs/user-guide/user-profile/), **Log out** sits
right under it, and the **API** link at the very bottom opens the
[API reference](/docs/api/) for your instance. Econumo can also install
itself as an app on your phone or computer — Settings offers an **Install the
app** row, and a banner may invite you to do the same.

**Note**
Transactions are kept on your device so accounts you've already seen load
instantly, and only accounts that changed are downloaded again. After an
upgrade to a new version (such as v1.8), a card at the bottom of the sidebar
links to its release notes; dismissing it on one device dismisses it
everywhere.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

---
## Installing Econumo as an app

Econumo can live on your home screen or in your Dock and open full-screen, like
any other app. When your browser supports it, **Settings** shows **Install the
app**; it opens your browser's install prompt or step-by-step instructions —
on an iPhone or iPad, for example, **Share → Add to Home Screen**.

Once installed, Econumo starts even without a connection.

---
## Working offline

Econumo keeps your recent data on the device, so you can keep going when the
connection drops: the sync button turns into a no-connection icon, and you can
still add, edit and delete transactions and change your budget plans. The
changes wait on the device and are sent when you are back online. The default
budget's previous, current and next months are kept for offline use; anything
that isn't stored on the device shows **Not available offline**.

If the server doesn't accept a change made offline, you'll find it in the
[Inbox](/docs/user-guide/inbox/#changes-that-werent-saved).

---

# Accounts

URL: https://econumo.com/docs/user-guide/accounts/

# Accounts

This section covers the basics of 'Accounts' in Econumo.

Accounts represent your accounts in financial institutions — for example,
"Savings account" or "Cash". Each account has its own currency, and accounts
are grouped into folders (such as "Personal" and "Family") that structure the
sidebar and the mobile home screen.

## In this section

- [Account creation](/docs/user-guide/accounts/#account-creation)
- [Managing your accounts](/docs/user-guide/accounts/#managing-your-accounts)
    - [Organize accounts in folders](/docs/user-guide/accounts/#organize-accounts-in-folders)
    - [Editing an account](/docs/user-guide/accounts/#editing-an-account)
- [Shared access](/docs/user-guide/accounts/#shared-access)

---

## Account creation

Open **Settings → Accounts** and press the **+** button on the folder you want
the account in. Specify the account name, current balance, currency, and icon.
The balance field comes with the same built-in calculator (`+`, `−`, `×`, `÷`,
`=`) as the [transaction dialog](/docs/user-guide/transactions/#adding-expenses).

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

**Note**
The starting balance is recorded as a regular transaction dated the day you
created the account, so your history starts consistent from day one.

---

## Managing your accounts

All your accounts are accessible via **Settings → Accounts**. This screen shows
every folder with its accounts, including the ones shared with you (marked with
the avatars of everyone who has access).

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

### Organize accounts in folders

Create folders with the **Create folder** button and drag accounts between them
using the dots handle next to their names. The folder structure is reflected in
the left sidebar on desktop and on the home screen on mobile.

Use the folder menu (the three dots on the folder row) to edit a folder's name,
move it up or down, or hide it. A hidden folder disappears from the main screen —
handy for accounts you rarely use — and can be shown again from the same menu.
Its accounts also stay out of the account pickers when you add or edit a
transaction or a recurring schedule; type three or more letters of an
account's name to find it anyway — it is marked **Hidden folder**. Its
[recurring schedules](/docs/user-guide/recurring-transactions/) still appear
in **Settings → Recurring transactions**, in a group marked **Hidden folder**.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

### Editing an account

Open the account menu to edit or delete an account. On desktop and tablet,
click the three dots next to the account; on mobile, tap the account row to
open its details.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

Editing lets you change the name, balance, currency, and icon. You can also
open the same dialog from the account page itself via the **Configure** button.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

**Note**
Correcting the balance in the edit dialog records a compensating transaction
for the difference, so your transaction history always adds up.

---

## Shared access

If you are [connected with your partner](/docs/user-guide/shared-access/), you
can share access to specific accounts. On desktop and tablet, choose **Access
control** in the account menu — or press the **Access control** button inside
the edit-account dialog — then select the person and the access level.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

Econumo offers three levels of shared access:

1. **View only** — the invited user can see only the balance and the
   transaction list.
2. **Manage transactions** — the invited user can also add, update, or delete
   transactions.
3. **Full control** — the invited user can manage all aspects of the account,
   including adding categories, tags, and payees on your behalf.

Granting access doesn't add the account to your partner's account list right
away: Econumo sends them a **pending invite** instead of sharing it outright.
They accept it — choosing which folder to file the account under — or decline
it, from their [Inbox](/docs/user-guide/inbox/) — see
[Shared Access](/docs/user-guide/shared-access/#accept-or-decline-a-sharing-request).
Until they respond, the Access control dialog shows **invitation pending**
next to their name. Once accepted, the shared account shows the avatars of
everyone who can use it — both in the sidebar and in **Settings → Accounts**.

---

# Transactions

URL: https://econumo.com/docs/user-guide/transactions/

# Transactions

This section provides an overview of Transactions in Econumo.

Transactions form the core of Econumo, as all budgeting is based on the
transactions you enter. Open any account to see its transaction list, search
it, and add new records. To find a transaction across all your accounts at
once, use [Search](/docs/user-guide/search/) (**Ctrl+K** / **⌘K**).

On an account page, drag the marker along the timeline above the list to
scroll through its history — the date shows as you drag — or click the marker
to jump straight to a month and year.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

The search field filters the transaction list as you type:

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

## In this section

- [Adding transactions](/docs/user-guide/transactions/#adding-transactions)
  - [Adding expenses](/docs/user-guide/transactions/#adding-expenses)
  - [Adding transfers](/docs/user-guide/transactions/#adding-transfers)
  - [Adding income](/docs/user-guide/transactions/#adding-income)
- [Reordering transactions](/docs/user-guide/transactions/#reordering-transactions)
- [Editing a transaction](/docs/user-guide/transactions/#editing-a-transaction)
- [Deleting a transaction](/docs/user-guide/transactions/#deleting-a-transaction)

**Note**
For payments that come back every month — rent, salary, a subscription — set up
a schedule once instead of typing them in again and again. See
[Recurring Transactions](/docs/user-guide/recurring-transactions/).

---

## Adding transactions

Press **Add transaction** on the account page (on mobile it is the button at
the bottom of the screen) to open the transaction dialog.

**Transaction date**

In the top-right corner of the dialog, you can set the transaction date (the
date you spent or earned the money). Clicking the date opens a calendar, and
the arrow next to it steps one day back. Note that transaction time is not
currently supported.

**Transaction types**

You can add one of the following transaction types:

- **Expense** (default option)
- **Transfer**
- **Income**

Each type has a different set of fields to complete.

---

### Adding expenses

To add an expense, pick the account, enter the amount, and choose a category —
that is all a record needs. Notes, a recipient, and tags are optional.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

**Amount**

Enter the amount spent in the account's currency. The `+`, `−`, `×`, `÷`, and
`=` buttons under the amount field (also available as keyboard keys on
desktop) let you calculate the total right in the dialog — for example, add up
several receipt lines and press `=`.

**Categories**

Categories are optional — you can save an expense without picking one. Click
the category field to search your categories or create a new one: type a name
that does not exist yet and press "Enter" (or "Search"/"Submit" on your mobile
keyboard). The name must be 3–64 characters long.

On desktop and tablet, the category field opens an inline dropdown under
itself: the first match is highlighted as you type, the arrow keys move the
highlight, and Enter picks it. On a phone it opens as a sheet instead, with
the category list above a search field pinned right above the keyboard, so
typing never pushes the list or the keyboard around.

**Note**
Leave a transaction uncategorized and it still counts toward your budget: it
shows up there as a read-only **Uncategorized** element instead of being left
out of the totals. See [Budgeting](/docs/user-guide/budgets/#budgeting).

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

**Recipients**

You can specify a recipient for each transaction — the name of a person or a
company where you spent the money. Like categories, recipients can be created
right from the dialog, and the field behaves the same way: an inline dropdown
on desktop and tablet, a sheet on a phone.

**Note**
Every searchable picker in the app opens as a phone sheet the same way —
accounts, the currency field in the account, budget, envelope and profile
forms, a budget's **Accounts** and **Savings accounts** lists, and **Merge
into…**.

**Tags**

Tags group spending across categories. The **Tags** row lists both kinds side
by side, and they behave differently when you tap them:

- **Budget tags**, marked with `#`, are for a project or an event — in the
  screenshots, the family tags its Italy vacation expenses with `Italy 2026`.
  A transaction takes only one, so picking a second replaces the first.
- **Reporting tags** track who or what the money went on — a kid, a pet, a
  second home. Toggle as many as apply.

Press the `+` button to create a new tag without leaving the dialog (3–64
characters); see
[Budget tags and reporting tags](/docs/user-guide/classifications/#budget-tags-and-reporting-tags)
for the difference in full.

**Notes**

The notes field allows you to add any comments related to the transaction.

---

### Adding transfers

Transfers move money between your accounts without affecting the budget:

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

**Note**
**Transfer** is greyed out in the transaction dialog unless you have at least
two visible accounts you can add transactions to — accounts in a hidden folder
don't count. Editing an existing transfer still works.

**From/To**

Select the account **from** which you want to move money **to** another
account. The swap button next to the account fields switches the direction.

**Amount**

Enter the transfer amount. The same in-dialog calculator (`+`, `−`, `×`, `÷`,
`=`) is available. If the two accounts use different currencies, a second field
appears so you can record the exact amount received in the target currency:

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

**Notes**

The notes field allows you to add any comments related to the transfer.

---

### Adding income

Recording an income works just like an expense: pick the account, enter the
amount, and choose an income category (income categories are separate from
expense categories). You can also set a **sender** — the person or company you
received the money from.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

---

## Reordering transactions

Put a day's transactions in the same order as your bank statement. On
desktop, hover a row and drag it by the grip that appears in place of its
icon. On a phone or tablet, press and hold a row, then drag it.

Dropping a row into another day moves it to that day and keeps its time. On a
transfer, each account keeps its own order, so reordering one side never
moves the other.

---

## Editing a transaction

On desktop and tablet, open the three-dots menu on a transaction row and choose
**Edit**. On mobile, tap the transaction to see its details, then press
**Edit**.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

The edit dialog is the same as the add dialog, pre-filled with the
transaction's data:

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

You can update any transaction in your own accounts, and in shared accounts
where you have at least **Manage transactions** access.

## Deleting a transaction

Choose **Delete** in the same menu (or in the details sheet on mobile) and
confirm. You can delete any transaction except transactions in view-only
accounts.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

---

# Recurring Transactions

URL: https://econumo.com/docs/user-guide/recurring-transactions/

# Recurring Transactions

Rent, salary, subscriptions, an annual insurance premium — payments that repeat
on a schedule don't need re-typing every time. Set them up once in
**Settings → Recurring transactions**, and Econumo keeps track of when each one
is next due.

Econumo never posts anything behind your back. The next occurrence shows up on
the account page as **Not posted**; you confirm it when the money actually
moves, or skip it when it doesn't. Either way the schedule rolls forward to the
following date.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

## In this section

- [Creating a recurring transaction](/docs/user-guide/recurring-transactions/#creating-a-recurring-transaction)
- [Posting or skipping a payment](/docs/user-guide/recurring-transactions/#posting-or-skipping-a-payment)
- [Editing and deleting a schedule](/docs/user-guide/recurring-transactions/#editing-and-deleting-a-schedule)

---

## Creating a recurring transaction

Open **Settings → Recurring transactions** and press **Add transaction** (on
mobile, the **+** button in the header). The dialog is the same one you use for
[ordinary transactions](/docs/user-guide/transactions/#adding-transactions),
with one extra field:

- **Type** — **Expense**, **Income**, or **Transfer**, chosen with the tabs at
  the top.
- **Date** — in the top-right corner. This is the date of the *next* payment;
  every following one is calculated from it.
- **Account**, **Amount** (with the same built-in calculator), **Category**,
  **Recipient** (**Sender** on an income schedule), **Tags**, and **Notes** —
  exactly as in a normal transaction.
- **Repeats** — how often the payment comes back: **Weekly**, **Every 2
  weeks**, **Monthly**, **Every 3 months**, or **Yearly**.

The list groups your schedules by account, showing the category and interval,
your notes and recipient, the amount, and the date the next payment falls due.

**Note**
Schedules follow the account, not the person. On a
[shared account](/docs/user-guide/shared-access/) everyone with access sees the
same schedules and can post or skip them — in the screenshots, the rent and the
grocery run on the Joint Account appear in both John's list and Megan's.
Schedules on your own accounts stay private to you.

---

## Posting or skipping a payment

The next occurrence of every schedule appears in its account's transaction
list, greyed out and labelled **Not posted**. It is a placeholder: it does not
affect your balance until you confirm it.

A schedule that is due today or overdue is pinned to the top of the account's
**Today** group, ahead of today's real transactions — so it reads as
something still waiting on you, not as something that already happened. A
schedule that is still ahead of its next date is untouched: it stays grouped
further down the list, at its own future date.

Select that row to open its **Transaction details**, which repeats the
schedule's interval at the bottom and offers two actions:

- **POST** — records the payment as a real transaction. Your balance and budget
  update, and the schedule moves on to the next date.
- **Skip** — the small step-over icon beside it. Passes on this occurrence
  without recording anything, and moves the schedule on to the next date.

The row's own three-dots menu is not the place to look: on a **Not posted**
placeholder it offers only **Edit** and **Delete**, both of which act on the
schedule rather than on this occurrence.

**Note**
A payment that is due or overdue shows its date in red, both in the list and on
the account page — a quick way to spot what is waiting for you.

You can also post a payment straight from **Settings → Recurring
transactions**: choose **Post** in the schedule's three-dots menu (on mobile,
tap the row to open the bottom sheet). The review dialog opens with its date
chip pre-filled to today for a due or overdue schedule — not the missed
scheduled date — though you can still edit it; a schedule that isn't overdue
keeps pre-filling its own scheduled date, as before.

Payments that are due today or overdue also collect in your
[Inbox](/docs/user-guide/inbox/), across all your accounts, under
**Scheduled transactions**. Select one there to open the same **Transaction
details** with **POST** and **Skip**, without going to the account first.

---

## Editing and deleting a schedule

Use the three-dots menu next to a schedule — on mobile, tap the row — and
choose **Edit** to change any of its fields, or **Delete** to remove the
schedule altogether.

Editing a schedule changes future payments only; transactions you have already
posted stay exactly as they were. Deleting a schedule likewise leaves posted
transactions untouched — it only stops future ones from being suggested.

---

# Search

URL: https://econumo.com/docs/user-guide/search/

# Search

One search box finds anything in Econumo: accounts, categories, payees, tags,
reporting tags and transactions. Open it from anywhere with **Ctrl+K**
(**⌘K** on a Mac), or with the magnifying-glass button at the top of the
sidebar (on mobile, at the top of the home screen).

Before you type, the search lists your most recent transactions, newest first:

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

## In this section

- [Finding things](/docs/user-guide/search/#finding-things)
- [Acting on a result](/docs/user-guide/search/#acting-on-a-result)

---

## Finding things

Start typing and the results group by kind — **Accounts**, **Categories**,
**Payees**, **Tags**, **Labels** (reporting tags), **Recurring** and
**Transactions** — with the best matches first.

You don't have to spell things exactly: missing letters are forgiven, so
*grcries* still finds **Groceries**, along with the transactions filed under
it. Amounts work too — type a figure the way it is stored or the way it is
displayed.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

The recent list leaves out transactions dated in the future, but a search
still finds them.

Search also finds your [recurring transactions](/docs/user-guide/recurring-transactions/),
under their own **Recurring** group — the next one due first, with its
schedule and next payment date. Searching for a payee, category, or tag also
surfaces the recurring payments that use it.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

**Note**
The same matcher drives every picker you can type into — the category, payee,
account and currency pickers in the transaction dialog and elsewhere — so a
typo there finds the right item too.

---

## Acting on a result

Pick a category, payee or tag to list its transactions right inside the
search window. Results also carry a three-dots menu with the actions that fit
them — for a category, **Edit**, **Archive**, **Merge into…** and **Delete**,
the same as in [Settings → Categories](/docs/user-guide/classifications/) — so
you can tidy up a duplicate the moment you spot it.

Click a **Recurring** result to open it: **Post** enters that payment now, the
button beside it skips it, and the **Recurring transaction** row opens the
schedule for editing — the same actions as the
[Recurring transactions](/docs/user-guide/recurring-transactions/) list.

---

# Inbox

URL: https://econumo.com/docs/user-guide/inbox/

# Inbox

The Inbox collects everything that is waiting on you in one place. Open it with
the tray icon at the top of the sidebar (on mobile, at the top of the home
screen); its badge shows how many things are waiting.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

## In this section

- [Scheduled transactions](/docs/user-guide/inbox/#scheduled-transactions)
- [Imported transactions](/docs/user-guide/inbox/#imported-transactions)
- [Changes that weren't saved](/docs/user-guide/inbox/#changes-that-werent-saved)
- [Sharing invites](/docs/user-guide/inbox/#sharing-invites)

With nothing pending, the page simply reads *"All caught up"*.

---

## Scheduled transactions

[Recurring transactions](/docs/user-guide/recurring-transactions/) that are
due today or overdue come first, across all your accounts. Each row shows the
schedule's category, interval, note, payee, amount and account, and when it
was due — *"Overdue · Nov 12"*.

Select a row to open its **Transaction details**, then:

- **POST** — records the payment as a real transaction, and the schedule
  moves on to its next date.
- **Skip** — the step-over icon beside it — passes on this occurrence without
  recording anything.

Either way the schedule moves on to its next date.

---

## Imported transactions

If you connect [Apple Wallet](/docs/user-guide/apple-wallet/) or
[SimpleFIN](/docs/user-guide/simplefin/), the Inbox also collects what the
import couldn't finish on its own:

- **Sync problems** — a SimpleFIN sync that failed or finished with errors,
  with the time of the last attempt.
- **Failed imports** and **To review** — transactions that couldn't go
  straight into an account, with the reason: a card or bank account that isn't
  mapped yet, an account you no longer have access to, or a currency without an
  exchange rate. **Import** one into an account, **Skip** it (skipped ones stay
  under **Skipped** and can be restored), **Retry** it, or **Discard** it.
- **Suggested rules** — [AI rule suggestions](/docs/user-guide/import-rules/#ai-rule-suggestions)
  for imported transactions that no rule classified.

---

## Changes that weren't saved

Econumo keeps working when you lose your connection: transactions you add,
edit or delete, and plan changes, wait on the device and are sent when you are
back online. If the server doesn't accept one of them, it lands under **Not
saved**, showing what the change was. **Try again** sends it once more;
**Discard** drops it.

---

## Sharing invites

When someone shares an [account](/docs/user-guide/accounts/#shared-access) or
a [budget](/docs/user-guide/budgets/#shared-access) with you, the invite waits
in the **Sharing** group at the bottom of the Inbox, saying who invited you
and to what. **Accept** it — for an account, you first choose the folder to
file it under — or **Decline** it. See
[Shared Access](/docs/user-guide/shared-access/#accept-or-decline-a-sharing-request)
for the details.

---

# Classifications

URL: https://econumo.com/docs/user-guide/classifications/

# Classifications

This section introduces the basics of 'Classifications' in Econumo, including
**Categories**, **Tags**, and **Payees**. All three entities share similar
functionality:

- Create a new item.
- Update or delete an existing item.
- Merge a duplicate into another item.
- Archive or unarchive any item.

**Categories** answer "what kind of spending is this?" — they're optional on a
transaction, but picking one is what makes a budget useful. **Tags** cut
across categories to group related spending (a trip, a renovation, the dog).
**Payees** record who you paid or who paid you.

## In this section

- [Create a category, tag, or payee](/docs/user-guide/classifications/#create-a-category-tag-or-payee)
- [Budget tags and reporting tags](/docs/user-guide/classifications/#budget-tags-and-reporting-tags)
- [Update or delete](/docs/user-guide/classifications/#update-or-delete)
- [Merge duplicates](/docs/user-guide/classifications/#merge-duplicates)
- [Archive or unarchive](/docs/user-guide/classifications/#archive-or-unarchive)
- [Searching a long list](/docs/user-guide/classifications/#searching-a-long-list)

---

## Create a category, tag, or payee

To create a new item, go to **Settings → Categories / Tags / Payees** and press
**Create category** / **Create tag** / **Create payee** (on mobile, the **+**
button in the header). Expense and income categories are listed separately:

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

You will need to fill out a few fields, such as:

- **Type** (income/expense) — only for categories
- **Icon** — only for categories
- **Kind** (reporting/budget) — only for tags, see
  [below](/docs/user-guide/classifications/#budget-tags-and-reporting-tags)
- **Name** (3–64 characters)

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

Payees need nothing but a name:

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

**Note**
You can also create categories, tags, and payees on the fly, right from the
[transaction dialog](/docs/user-guide/transactions/#adding-expenses) — no trip
to Settings required.

---

## Budget tags and reporting tags

Tags come in two kinds, and the **New tag** dialog asks which one you are
making before anything else:

- **Budget tag** — *"Plan a project or event. Only one tag per transaction."*
  A vacation, a wedding, a renovation. Because a transaction can carry only
  one, its spending adds up cleanly, so a budget tag gets a row in your
  [budget](/docs/user-guide/budgets/) with a limit of its own. Budget tags are
  marked with `#`.
- **Reporting tag** — *"Analyse what the money went on. Several tags per
  transaction allowed."* A kid, a dog, a second home. A transaction can carry
  as many as you like, so the totals deliberately overlap and take no part in
  the budget maths. Reporting tags show up in their own
  [Reporting tags block](/docs/user-guide/budgets/#reporting-tags) at the foot
  of the budget page.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

The Tags screen keeps the two apart in **BUDGET TAGS** and **REPORTING TAGS**
sections:

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

**Note**
A tag's kind is fixed when you create it and cannot be changed afterwards. If
you picked the wrong one, create the tag you meant and
[merge](/docs/user-guide/classifications/#merge-duplicates) the other into it.

---

## Update or delete

On desktop and tablet, click the three dots next to an item and select **Edit**
or **Delete**. On mobile, tap the item to open the same actions in a bottom
sheet.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

Deleting an item will remove it from all transactions and budgets.

Use **Reorder list** to change the order in which items appear in pickers and
in the budget.

---

## Merge duplicates

Long-lived data collects duplicates: a "Groceries" and a "Food", two spellings
of the same shop. **Merge into…** in the same three-dots menu folds one into
another instead of deleting it and losing the history.

1. Open **Settings → Categories** (or **Tags**, or **Payees**).
2. Choose **Merge into…** in the duplicate's menu. On a phone the same dialog
   arrives as a bottom sheet.
3. Pick the survivor from the list, or find it with the **Search** box. The
   dialog spells out what will happen: *"All transactions from … will be
   moved, and … will be deleted."*
4. Press **MERGE**.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

Every transaction pointing at the duplicate is moved to the survivor, and the
duplicate is then deleted.

**Note**
Merging two categories also merges their budget rows: the planned amounts are
**added together** per period rather than thrown away. The dialog says so
before you commit — *"If the two sit in different envelopes, update your
budget first so you don't lose your planned amounts — limits are added
together when merging."*

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

---

## Archive or unarchive

You can archive items that are no longer relevant to you. Archived items won't
appear in the transaction dialog but will still be visible in the transaction
list, and in a budget if you've budgeted them or had any associated spending.

Use the switch on the right side of each element to archive or unarchive it.
The **Active only** toggle at the top of the list controls whether archived
items are shown.

---

## Searching a long list

Press the search icon next to the page heading to reveal a filter field —
handy once your list of categories, tags, or payees grows past a quick scan.
It filters the list as you type.

---

# Budgets

URL: https://econumo.com/docs/user-guide/budgets/

# Budgets

This section introduces the basics of 'Budgets' in Econumo.

Budgets enable you to implement a "Cash Stuffing" method, also known as the
envelope budgeting approach, which uses envelopes to manage spending.

The concept is straightforward: take a few envelopes, label each with an
expense category — such as groceries, rent, or car loan — and place the amount
of money you plan to spend in each envelope. This way, you set limits on your
spending for each category.

Econumo allows you to create virtual envelopes and allocate your funds
accordingly, so you can easily track how much money remains for each specific
category:

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

## In this section

- [Budget creation](/docs/user-guide/budgets/#budget-creation)
  - [Month start day](/docs/user-guide/budgets/#month-start-day)
- [Update budget details](/docs/user-guide/budgets/#update-budget-details)
- [Manage your budget](/docs/user-guide/budgets/#manage-your-budget)
  - [Budgeting](/docs/user-guide/budgets/#budgeting)
  - [Savings accounts](/docs/user-guide/budgets/#savings-accounts)
  - [Organizing your budget](/docs/user-guide/budgets/#organizing-your-budget)
  - [Work with the budget](/docs/user-guide/budgets/#work-with-the-budget)
  - [Comments](/docs/user-guide/budgets/#comments)
- [Budgets list](/docs/user-guide/budgets/#budgets-list)
- [Completing, duplicating and archiving a budget](/docs/user-guide/budgets/#completing-duplicating-and-archiving-a-budget)
- [Shared access](/docs/user-guide/budgets/#shared-access)

**Note**
To plan several months at once instead of one at a time, switch the budget to
its [Plan view](/docs/user-guide/plan/) with the **Budget** / **Plan** tabs
beside the months bar — the same budget laid out as a month-by-month sheet.

---

## Budget creation

Open **Settings → Budgets & Plans** and press **Create budget** (on mobile, the
**+** button in the header). Give the budget a name, pick its base currency,
choose the **Month start day**, and switch on the accounts that take part in
it — the counter above the list
keeps track (*"3 of 5 included"*). Once accounts are in, **Savings accounts**
lets you mark some of them as
[savings](/docs/user-guide/budgets/#savings-accounts).

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

**Note**
Account membership is an explicit list, and a new budget starts with every
switch off — turn on the accounts you actually budget from. Budgets start from
the current month.

### Month start day

Budget months don't have to follow the calendar. Pick any day from **1** to
**28** as the **Month start day** to run the budget from payday to payday. Each
month is named after the month it starts in: with day 25, *November* covers
25 November to 24 December. The months bar and the
[Plan view](/docs/user-guide/plan/) show each month's dates under its name.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

The start day belongs to the budget, so everyone sharing it sees the same
months. You can change it later in
[Budget settings](/docs/user-guide/budgets/#update-budget-details) — your plans
stay on their months, and only the dates each month covers change. Only the
budget's owner, or someone with full control of it, can change the start day.

**Note**
Reports, recurring schedules, account pages and CSV exports keep using
calendar months.

---
## Update budget details

Open your budget and press **Configure** in the top-right corner. On desktop it
opens **Budget settings** straight away; on a tablet or a phone it opens a
short menu — choose **Budget settings** there. In the dialog you can rename
the budget, change its currency and its
[month start day](/docs/user-guide/budgets/#month-start-day), add or remove
accounts, and choose which of them are savings accounts:

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

An account that already carries transactions in past months of this budget
cannot be removed from it — taking it out would rewrite months you have
already closed. The dialog says so under the list.

A note under the accounts reminds you that
[debts](/docs/user-guide/debts/) in this budget are shown by name, with their
payments and balances, to everyone who has access to it.

The other entry in the tablet and phone **Configure** menu, **Edit
structure**, is described in
[Organizing your budget](/docs/user-guide/budgets/#organizing-your-budget).

---
## Manage your budget

The budget page has three sections, in the same order on every screen size:

- **Income** — what you expect to earn: **Planned**, **Received** and what
  is still **To receive**.
- **Savings** — your [savings accounts](/docs/user-guide/budgets/#savings-accounts):
  **Planned**, **Saved** and the **Balance** at month end.
- **Expenses** — what you plan to spend: **Budget**, **Spent** and
  **Available**.

Underneath sit the totals for the month, ending with your **Balance at month
end**.

Inside the sections you work with these entities:

- **Budget Folders** — to organize your spending conveniently (in the
  screenshots: _Essentials_, _Lifestyle_, _Vacations_).
- **Categories** — your Econumo categories.
- **Tags** — your budget [tags](/docs/user-guide/classifications/). These
  aggregate spending across categories (e.g. the whole _Italy 2026_ vacation).
  Reporting tags are not budgeted; they get
  [their own block](/docs/user-guide/budgets/#reporting-tags) at the foot of
  the page.
- **Envelopes** — these group several categories into one limit (e.g. an
  envelope for _Food_ could contain _Groceries_, _Drinks_, and _Restaurants_).
  Both Income and Expenses can hold envelopes.
- **Debts** — an expense category or envelope that tracks a loan shows the
  payments left and its payoff date under its name. See
  [Debts](/docs/user-guide/debts/).

---
### Budgeting

The goal of budgeting is to maintain your monthly budget. Ideally, you should
prepare your budget before the month starts and make minor adjustments during
the month as needed. The months bar at the top switches between periods — on
desktop and tablet the **‹** and **›** arrows beside it step through the
months — and the budget shows how much money remains in your virtual
envelopes. The bar is clamped to the budget's own lifetime: an open budget runs
well into the future, while a
[completed one](/docs/user-guide/budgets/#completing-duplicating-and-archiving-a-budget)
stops just past its final month.

Each expense row has three columns:

1. **Budget** — the amount you plan to spend this month. A small figure in
   front of it, such as `-1,923.02 +`, is what is left from earlier months.
2. **Spent** — the amount you have actually spent.
3. **Available** — what is left: the budgeted amount plus anything carried
   over. It shows as a green pill, or a red one when the row is overspent.

On desktop, click a number in the **Budget** column to change it. The amount
field takes the same calculator keypad (`+`, `−`, `×`, `÷`, `=`) as the
[transaction dialog](/docs/user-guide/transactions/#adding-expenses); press
**Save**. On a tablet or a phone, tap the row's figures to open its sheet and
press **Set budget**:

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

From the current month on, setting an expense row's amount shows a **Coming
up** list: the recurring payments still due that month, plus any of the row's
transactions already dated later in the month, each converted to the row's
currency. The list ends with **Already spent** (if you've already spent something)
and a **Total** line. Tap or click the list to put that total into the amount
field — adjust it if you like, then save.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

The same list appears in the [Plan](/docs/user-guide/plan/) grid's cell
editor. **Spent**, **Actual** and **Available** always count only real
transactions — Coming up is a hint, not a figure of its own — but for an
expense row, a plan below what's already spent plus what's still due shows in
red.

On a phone the budget is a single-month view. Each row shows **Budget** and
**Spent**, with a thin progress bar under it that turns red once spending runs
past the budget. Tap a row's figures to open its sheet: the month's figures,
the latest comment, **Transactions** to list what was spent, and **Set
budget** (**Set plan** on a savings row). The pencil icon in the sheet's
header edits the item itself. On a tablet, the desktop-style rows open the
same sheet when you tap their figures:

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

If a [transaction has no category](/docs/user-guide/transactions/#adding-expenses),
its amount still counts: it appears as a read-only **Uncategorized** line at
the end of the Income or Expenses section — no **Budget** or **Available**
figure, just the amount — instead of being silently left out. Assign a
category to those transactions and they move into the rows above.

---
### Savings accounts

Money you move into a savings account isn't spent — it's saved. Mark any of
the budget's accounts as savings in **Budget settings → Savings accounts**
(the **Savings** section's three-dots menu has a shortcut to the same list):

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

Each savings account gets its own row in the **Savings** section:

- **Planned** — how much you mean to put away this month.
- **Saved** — the account's whole net change for the month: transfers in and
  out, interest and fees.
- **Balance** — the account's balance at the end of the month. For future
  months it is projected from your plans.

The totals under the budget add a **Savings** line for the month and a **Total
savings** line for the combined balance.

The savings flag belongs to the budget, not to the account, so the same
account can be savings in one budget and everyday money in another. Turning an
account's savings flag off deletes the planned amounts and comments of its
savings row in this budget; the saved amounts and the transactions themselves
are not touched.

---
### Organizing your budget

You change the structure right on the budget page.

**On desktop**, hover a row: a drag handle appears on its left and a
three-dots menu beside its name. Drag rows and folders by the handle to
reorder them or move them between folders, and use the menus for everything
else.

**On a tablet or a phone**, press **Configure** and choose **Edit structure**.
Every row then shows its handle and three-dots menu; press **Done editing**
when you are finished.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

The menus offer:

- **Income** and **Expenses** section headers — **Create folder**, **New
  envelope**, **New category**, and, on the Expenses section, **New tag**.
- A **folder** — **New envelope**, **New category**, **New tag** on an
  expense folder, **Edit** (rename), and **Delete folder**.
- A **category, tag or envelope** — **Edit**, **Change currency**, **Move to
  folder…**, **Archive**, **Merge into…** and **Delete**.

**Note**
Creating a tag this way places it at the top of that section or folder.

An action you can't take right now is greyed out and says why — a folder that
still holds items reads **Delete folder (not empty)**, and an item you don't
own reads **(no access)**:

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

Items that are not in any folder collect under **No folder** at the end of
their section.

**Envelopes.** Choose **New envelope** in a section or folder menu. Pick a
name, currency, icon, and the categories you want to include:

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

Deleting an envelope releases its categories back into the budget.

**Element currency.** Each element can be budgeted in its own currency: open
the element's three-dots menu and choose **Change currency**. Amounts spent
and available for that element are converted automatically.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

---
### Work with the budget

#### Tag and envelope breakdown

Tags and envelopes aggregate several categories. Expand one by clicking its
name to see where the money actually went.

In a shared budget, you and your partner often keep your own tag with the
same name — in the screenshots, both John and Megan tag their Italy trip
spending `Italy 2026`. Same-name tags show as a single line, such as
**Italy 2026 · 2 tags**, with the combined **Budget**, **Spent** and
**Available**. Expand it to see each person's own tag, with their name next
to it:

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

Expand a tag itself to see the categories its spending went to:

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

**Note**
Grouping is display only: each tag keeps its own limit, and nothing is
merged. The same grouping and expansion works in the
[Plan](/docs/user-guide/plan/) grid.

#### Spending details

To see the transactions behind any number, click the amount in the **Spent**
column (on a phone, open the row's sheet and press **Transactions**):

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

#### Reporting tags

Below the expenses — under the **Uncategorized** line — sits a separate
**Reporting tags** block. It totals what you spent per
[reporting tag](/docs/user-guide/classifications/#budget-tags-and-reporting-tags)
in the month: people, pets, places. Expand the block by clicking its title,
and expand a single tag to see the categories behind its total.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

These rows show a **Spent** figure only — no **Budget**, no **Available** — and
they sit outside the budget's totals. That is deliberate: a transaction can
carry several reporting tags at once, so its full amount counts under each of
them, and adding the block into the budget maths would count the same money
twice. Use it to answer "what did the dog cost us this month?", not "how much
is left to spend?".

#### Multi-currency budgets

Elements budgeted in a foreign currency are converted to the budget's currency
for folder and budget totals. See
[Multi-Currency](/docs/user-guide/multi-currency/#currency-in-your-budget) for
the full picture.

---
### Comments

Any budget cell — one item in one month — can carry a comment thread: a note
like "trip to Lisbon" or "new TV" that explains a number. A small coloured
triangle in the cell's corner marks the cells that have one; on desktop,
hovering it previews the latest comments.

Click the marker to open the thread, type in **Comment** (up to 500
characters), and press **Post**. On a phone, the row's sheet shows the latest
comment — tap **Comments (N)** to open the whole thread. In the
[Plan view](/docs/user-guide/plan/) you can also open a selected cell's thread
with **Shift+F2**.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

Everyone with access to the budget can read the comments and add their own —
including people you shared it with as **View only**.

---
## Budgets list

You can access your budgets list at **Settings → Budgets & Plans**. Shared budgets show the avatars of everyone
who uses them, and the bookmark icon marks your default budget — the one that
opens from **Budget & Plan** in the sidebar. Budgets you have archived collapse
into an **Archived (N)** group at the bottom of the list:

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

---
## Completing, duplicating and archiving a budget

A budget does not have to run forever. Every budget's three-dots menu in
**Settings → Budgets & Plans** carries its whole life cycle: **Open budget**,
**Access control**, **Duplicate…**, **Complete…**, **Archive**, and **Delete**.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

### Complete a budget

**Complete…** closes a budget off at a chosen month. Pick the **Last month** it
covers; leave **Continue in a copy starting this month** on to name and start
its successor in the same step, with **Copy plans** deciding whether the
planned amounts come along. Turn that switch off and the **Copy plans** and
**Name** fields disappear — the budget is simply closed, with no successor.
Press **SAVE** and the budget is archived straight away: it leaves the active
list immediately and joins the **Archived** group below it.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

### Duplicate a budget

**Duplicate…** copies a budget on its own, without closing the original: its
structure, folders, envelopes, member accounts and sharing all come across. The
copy is pre-named after the original with *"(copy)"* appended, keeps **Copy
plans** on, and can **Start from this month** instead of the original's first
month.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

### Archive and unarchive

**Archive** files a budget away without completing it. An archived budget stays
in the list under **Archived (N)** and stays fully browsable — opening it shows
a banner reading *"This budget is archived and read-only"*, and its numbers
stay exactly as they were. Its menu offers **Unarchive** in place of
**Archive**, which brings it back to the active list.

---
## Shared access

To budget together with your partner, you first need to
[connect with them](/docs/user-guide/shared-access/). Then open the budgets
list, click the three dots on the budget you wish to share, and select
**Access control**. Pick the person and the access level:

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

Econumo supports the following access levels for budgets:

- **View only** — you share your budget only for viewing.
- **Manage budget** — you and your partner can collaboratively manage this
  budget and contribute to it together.
- **Full control** — like Manage budget, but your partner can also delete and
  rename the budget.

As with accounts, this sends a **pending invite** rather than sharing the
budget outright — your partner accepts or declines it from their
[Inbox](/docs/user-guide/inbox/), as described in
[Shared Access](/docs/user-guide/shared-access/#accept-or-decline-a-sharing-request).
Once accepted, your partner sees the budget in their own budget list, and you
budget the same envelopes together — as John and Megan do with the "Family
budget" in the screenshots throughout this page.

---

# Plan

URL: https://econumo.com/docs/user-guide/plan/

# Plan

The [budget](/docs/user-guide/budgets/) shows one month at a time: what you
planned, what you spent, what is left. The **Plan** view shows the same budget
as a spreadsheet across several months — one row per envelope, category, tag
or savings account, one column per month — so you can put next spring's
holiday or an annual insurance premium into the plan long before the money
moves.

Both views belong to the same budget. Switching between them changes nothing
about your data; it only changes how much of the budget you are looking at.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

## In this section

- [Opening the Plan view](/docs/user-guide/plan/#opening-the-plan-view)
- [Reading the sheet](/docs/user-guide/plan/#reading-the-sheet)
- [Planning a month](/docs/user-guide/plan/#planning-a-month)
- [Copying an amount forward](/docs/user-guide/plan/#copying-an-amount-forward)
- [Adding up a selection](/docs/user-guide/plan/#adding-up-a-selection)
- [The Balance row](/docs/user-guide/plan/#the-balance-row)
- [Keeping a long sheet readable](/docs/user-guide/plan/#keeping-a-long-sheet-readable)

---

## Opening the Plan view

Open your budget from **Budget & Plan** in the sidebar, then switch the
**Budget** / **Plan** tabs beside the months bar to **Plan**. The Plan view
works on desktop and on a tablet.

On a phone there is no grid: the budget stays a single-month view, and you
plan a month from each row's sheet — tap the row's figures and press **Set
budget** (**Set plan** on a savings row). See
[Budgeting](/docs/user-guide/budgets/#budgeting).

---

## Reading the sheet

Rows are the elements of your budget, in the structure you gave it, under the
same **Income**, **Savings** and **Expenses** sections as the budget view.
[Same-name tags](/docs/user-guide/budgets/#tag-and-envelope-breakdown) from
different budget partners group into one row here too, such as **Italy 2026 ·
2 tags** — expand it to see each tag on its own.

Each cell shows the amount actually spent or earned on the left, in small grey
type, next to the amount you planned. An actual figure that overshoots the
plan is shown in red. On a savings row, the small figure is the account's
balance at the end of that month.

A blank cell means no plan is set for that month and nothing happened. A plan
of exactly zero is different from no plan at all: type `0` into a cell to
keep it visible — handy for a category, tag or envelope you haven't used yet
but want to see in the sheet — and it still turns red once a recurring
payment comes due against it.

Click an actual figure to list that month's transactions behind it.

The **‹** and **›** arrows above the sheet move the visible window to earlier
and later months.

---

## Planning a month

The sheet works like a spreadsheet:

1. Click a cell to select it, or move to it with the arrow keys.
2. Type the amount, or press **F2** to edit the amount already there.
3. Press **Enter** to save, or **Escape** to leave the cell as it was.

**Delete** clears a cell's plan entirely — the cell goes blank, not to zero —
and you can paste an amount copied from elsewhere.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

Income rows are planned exactly the same way — a planned salary is what makes
the projection at the foot of the sheet worth reading. A selected cell with a
[comment](/docs/user-guide/budgets/#comments) opens its thread with
**Shift+F2**.

---

## Copying an amount forward

Most plans repeat: the same rent, the same phone bill, month after month. When
a cell is selected, a small square appears at its bottom-right corner —
**Copy budget to the following months**. Drag it to the right to repeat that
amount across the months it covers. Dragging or copying a blank cell clears
the months it covers instead of writing a zero into them.

---

## Adding up a selection

On desktop you can select several cells at once — drag across them,
**Shift**+click the far corner of a range, or **Ctrl**+click (**⌘**+click on a
Mac) to add single cells. A small label under the selection adds them up: how
many cells, their **Plan** total and their **Actual** total.

---

## The Balance row

The foot of the sheet sums each month: **Income**, **Expenses**, **Savings**
and **Total savings**, with the **Balance** row pinned underneath. Balance
rolls your money forward month by month, starting from your real account
balances, so each column shows what you would be left with by the end of that
month if the plan holds.

That is what makes planning ahead useful: put a two-week trip into next July and
you can see immediately what it does to the months after it.

---

## Keeping a long sheet readable

A budget with a few dozen elements makes for a tall sheet. A few things help:

- The **Income**, **Savings** and **Expenses** headers, and each folder
  header, collapse with the chevron beside them. The Plan view remembers its
  own folding, separately from the budget view.
- The **Σ** button on a section or folder header shows that group's sums on
  its header row.
- Drag the right edge of the name column to make it wider or narrower;
  double-click the edge to reset it.

---

# Debts

URL: https://econumo.com/docs/user-guide/debts/

# Debts

A debt tracks a loan — a mortgage, a car loan, a student loan — inside your
[budget](/docs/user-guide/budgets/), without opening an account for it. Your
net worth and account totals stay clean, and the budget still shows how the
loan is going: how many payments are left, how much of each payment is
interest, and when the loan will be paid off.

A debt sits on an expense category (or an envelope). The expenses you already
record in that category are its payments, so nothing changes in how you enter
or import transactions. Each payment is split bank-style into **interest** and
**principal**, and Econumo works out the rate your lender is charging from the
loan's terms — you never have to type it in.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

## In this section

- [Tracking a loan as a debt](/docs/user-guide/debts/#tracking-a-loan-as-a-debt)
- [Debt details](/docs/user-guide/debts/#debt-details)
  - [Overview](/docs/user-guide/debts/#overview)
  - [Balance](/docs/user-guide/debts/#balance)
  - [Settings](/docs/user-guide/debts/#settings)
  - [Paying off or deleting a debt](/docs/user-guide/debts/#paying-off-or-deleting-a-debt)
- [Debts in your budget and plan](/docs/user-guide/debts/#debts-in-your-budget-and-plan)
- [Debts in a shared budget](/docs/user-guide/debts/#debts-in-a-shared-budget)

---

## Tracking a loan as a debt

Give the loan its own expense category first (for example _Car Loan_) and
record its payments there, from an account that belongs to the budget. Then,
on the budget page:

1. Open the category row's **⋮** menu and choose **Track as debt**. On a
   tablet or a phone, press **Configure → Edit structure** first — the rows
   get their **⋮** menus there.
2. Enter the regular **Payment** — Econumo suggests the amount planned for the
   row — and how often it **Repeats** (every week, every 2 weeks, every month,
   every quarter or every year).
3. Press **Add**.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

The debt starts collecting its payments straight away. To see the balance, the
payments left and the payoff date, finish setting it up: open
[Debt details](/docs/user-guide/debts/#debt-details), go to **Settings**, and
enter the **Amount borrowed**, the **Start date** (when the loan began) and the
**Last payment date** (when the loan ends).

**Note**
Only expenses on the budget's own accounts count as payments. If you pay the
loan from an account that isn't part of the budget, add that account in
[Budget settings](/docs/user-guide/budgets/#update-budget-details) first.

---

## Debt details

Open the debt row's **⋮** menu and choose **Debt → Debt details**. On a phone,
tap the row and then **Debt details** in its sheet. The details open in a
dialog with four tabs.

### Overview

The top shows how many payments are left, with a bar for the payments made so
far (*"6 of 45 paid"*). Under it, **Loan** lists the balance today and the rate
Econumo worked out, the amount borrowed and when, the payment and how often it
repeats, the next and the last payment, and how much you have paid — and still
plan to pay — on top of the schedule. **Payments** lists every payment with its
interest, principal and the balance after it; **Show future payments** adds
the schedule ahead.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

### Balance

**Balance today** compares Econumo's figure with your bank statement. When your
lender sends a statement, press **Add a statement** and enter the balance it
shows; Econumo uses it from that date on. **Rate today** shows the rate and the
payment in force. If your lender changes the rate, press **Add a rate change**.

### Settings

The loan's terms: **Amount borrowed**, **Start date**, **Last payment date**,
**Payment** and **Repeats**. Correct them here if you entered something wrong;
Econumo splits every payment again with the new terms.

### Paying off or deleting a debt

The **Danger zone** tab has two buttons:

- **Mark as paid off** sets what is owed to zero and stops counting down the
  payments — use it when you settle the last small amount.
- **Delete** removes the debt and its history. Your transactions are not
  changed.

Both are also in the row's **⋮** menu under **Debt**.

---

## Debts in your budget and plan

A debt stays in its row. Under the name it shows the payments left and the
payoff date (*"40 payments left · Paid off by Feb 2030"*), and its **Budget**
and **Spent** columns work like any other row.

Plan the debt as you would any category, in the budget or the
[Plan view](/docs/user-guide/plan/). Planning more than the scheduled payment
counts as an extra payment: the payoff date moves earlier, and the overview
shows it under **Planned extra**.

---

## Debts in a shared budget

Everyone with access to the budget sees each debt by name, with its payments
and balance — the **Budget settings** dialog says so under the accounts. People
who can manage the budget can also open and change its details; with view-only
access, you can look but not edit.

---

# Reports

URL: https://econumo.com/docs/user-guide/reports/

# Reports

Reports answer bigger questions than a single month's budget. Open them with
the chart icon at the bottom of the sidebar, next to the sync button (on
mobile, at the bottom of the home screen).

The first screen is a list of reports to choose from. The picker in its
top-right corner sets the **scope**: **My accounts**, or one of your budgets —
a shared budget covers everyone taking part in it. Each report card previews
its answer; **Net worth** shows today's total and how much it changed this
year.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

## In this section

- [Net worth](/docs/user-guide/reports/#net-worth)
- [Report tabs](/docs/user-guide/reports/#report-tabs)
- [Suggest a report](/docs/user-guide/reports/#suggest-a-report)

---

## Net worth

**Net worth** answers *"Am I getting richer or poorer?"*. It draws one line
for the total of your accounts over time, with the change for the period
underneath. Pick the period with **1y**, **3y** or **All** — **All** starts
at your first transaction.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

The table under the chart shows where the change came from, with **Start**,
**Now** and **Change** columns:

- For **My accounts**, one row per account folder; open a folder to see its
  accounts.
- For a budget, one row per person taking part in it. Open a row to see that
  person's savings accounts by name, plus one **Everyday accounts** total for
  the rest. Another person's accounts that aren't shared with you are never
  listed one by one — only their total.

Select an account row to list its transactions.

To look at a shorter stretch, **drag across the chart**. The figures follow
your selection, which replaces the period buttons, and a **Transactions**
button lists what happened in that range.

**Note**
Deleted accounts are left out of the report completely, including their
history.

---

## Report tabs

Reports open in tabs at the top of the page, so you can keep several open side
by side — for example, net worth for your own accounts in one tab and for the
family budget in another. **+** opens a new tab with the report list. A tab's
menu can rename, duplicate or close it. Tabs are remembered on the device you
use.

---

## Suggest a report

Missing a report you need? The **Suggest a report** card opens the feedback
form with **Feature request** already chosen. Tell us what you'd like to see.

---

# Shared Access

URL: https://econumo.com/docs/user-guide/shared-access/

# Shared Access

This section provides an overview of Shared Access in Econumo.

Econumo enables users to connect with each other to share access to various
accounts and budgets — the foundation for family budgeting. Connections are
managed in **Settings → Shared access**:

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

## In this section

- [Connect with another user](/docs/user-guide/shared-access/#connect-with-another-user)
- [Accept or decline a sharing request](/docs/user-guide/shared-access/#accept-or-decline-a-sharing-request)
- [Remove connection between users](/docs/user-guide/shared-access/#remove-connection-between-users)
- [Check shared accounts and budgets](/docs/user-guide/shared-access/#check-shared-accounts-and-budgets)
- [Access status](/docs/user-guide/shared-access/#access-status)

---

## Connect with another user

When you connect with another Econumo user, you aren't sharing anything yet.
You will specify which accounts and budgets to share later.

To connect, go to **Settings → Shared access** and press **Create invitation**.
You will get a short code that is valid for 5 minutes:

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

Ask your partner to open Econumo, navigate to **Settings → Shared access**,
press **Accept invitation**, and enter the code:

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

After the invitation is accepted, you will see each other in the connections
list, and you can start sharing
[accounts](/docs/user-guide/accounts/#shared-access) and
[budgets](/docs/user-guide/budgets/#shared-access).

---

## Accept or decline a sharing request

Sharing an account or budget with someone doesn't hand it over immediately —
Econumo sends a **pending invite** that the other person has to accept or
decline first. Invites land in your [Inbox](/docs/user-guide/inbox/) — the
tray icon at the top of the sidebar (on mobile, at the top of the home
screen), whose badge counts everything waiting on you. Sharing invites sit in
the **Sharing** group at the bottom of the Inbox, each one saying who invited
you and whether it is an **Account** or a **Budget**.

For each request:

- **Accept** — for an account, you first choose which folder to file it
  under (or leave it in **General**, which is created automatically if it
  doesn't exist yet); a budget is added straight to your budgets list.
- **Decline** — Econumo asks you to confirm, then the invite is dismissed.

While a request is still pending, the person who sent it sees
**invitation pending** next to your name in the Access control dialog.

**Note**
Connections and shares that already existed before this flow shipped keep
working without any action on your part — Econumo grandfathered them in as
already accepted.

---

## Remove connection between users

You can delete the connection between users at any time: open the three-dots
menu next to the connection and choose **Delete**. Econumo asks you to confirm
first, because this action removes all shared access for accounts and budgets
in both directions:

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

The connection's dialog (described below) also has a **Delete** button that
removes the connection the same way.

---

## Check shared accounts and budgets

To view everything you share with a user, choose **View** in the connection's
menu (on mobile, tap the connection). The dialog lists all shared budgets and
accounts, who owns each item, and the current access level:

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

Select an item in this dialog — this is also the way to manage access from a
phone. What opens depends on which side you're on:

- For something **you own**, you get an access-level picker where you can
  change the level or press **Revoke access**.
- For something **shared with you**, you get a plain confirmation to
  **Decline access** instead.

The dialog lists only items that are already shared; sharing a new account or
budget is done with **Access control**, as described in the
[Accounts](/docs/user-guide/accounts/#shared-access) and
[Budgets](/docs/user-guide/budgets/#shared-access) sections.

---

## Access status

Econumo can restrict an account to read-only — for example when a
trial period runs out.
Read access, including exporting your data, keeps working; adding or changing
anything is disabled until access is restored. A connection in this state
shows a **Read-only** badge (or a countdown, e.g. **Subscription ends in 5
days**) next to their name in **Settings → Shared access**, along with a
**Manage subscription** link where a billing portal is configured.

---

# Multi-Currency

URL: https://econumo.com/docs/user-guide/multi-currency/

# Multi-Currency

Econumo lets you keep accounts in different currencies and still budget across
all of them. Each account has one fixed currency; transfers between currencies
record both amounts, and your budget converts everything to a single currency
so the totals add up.

In the examples on this page, John's family keeps most accounts in US dollars
but also has a **Euro Cash** account they top up before travelling to Italy.

## In this section

- [Accounts in different currencies](/docs/user-guide/multi-currency/#accounts-in-different-currencies)
- [Cross-currency transfers](/docs/user-guide/multi-currency/#cross-currency-transfers)
- [Currency in your budget](/docs/user-guide/multi-currency/#currency-in-your-budget)

**Note**
Which currencies you can pick from is up to you: choose them in
**Settings → Currencies**, where you can also add
[a currency of your own](/docs/user-guide/currencies/#adding-your-own-currency)
with a rate you set. The currencies your server ships with, and how their
exchange rates are kept up to date, are configured by whoever runs your Econumo
instance — see [Multi-Currency Support](/docs/self-hosting/multi-currency/) in
the self-hosting docs.

---

## Accounts in different currencies

An account's currency is chosen when you
[create it](/docs/user-guide/accounts/#account-creation) and shown next to its
balance everywhere in the app. Every transaction on that account is entered in
the account's own currency — the Euro Cash account below is in EUR, so its
balance and all its transactions are in euros.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

To spend from an account, add the transaction in that account's currency. To
move money between currencies, use a transfer.

---

## Cross-currency transfers

When you [transfer](/docs/user-guide/transactions/#adding-transfers) between two
accounts that use different currencies, Econumo shows **two amount fields** —
one for the source currency and one for the destination — so you can record
exactly what left one account and what arrived in the other. This keeps both
balances correct regardless of the rate your bank used.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

In the Euro Cash account above, the "Transfer from John's Card" line is the
euro side of one such transfer — dollars left the card, euros arrived in the
cash account.

---

## Currency in your budget

A budget is kept in a single base currency — the code above the first column
of the budget, `USD` in the screenshots — but individual elements (categories,
tags, envelopes) can be budgeted in their own currency. Open the element's
three-dots menu and choose **Change currency**. On desktop the menu appears
when you hover the row; on a tablet or a phone, turn on **Configure → Edit
structure** first.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

Spending in a foreign currency is converted to the budget's currency for folder
and budget totals.

**Note**
Conversions use the exchange rates loaded into your Econumo instance. If rates
look off, ask your administrator to refresh them (see
[Multi-Currency Support](/docs/self-hosting/multi-currency/)).

---

# Currencies

URL: https://econumo.com/docs/user-guide/currencies/

# Currencies

**Settings → Currencies** controls which currencies Econumo offers you when you
create an account, a budget, or a budget element. It holds two kinds of
currency:

- **Econumo currencies** — the ones that ship with your server. They are
  available to everyone on the instance, and their exchange rates are managed
  centrally and refresh automatically when the server has rate updates
  configured.
- **My currencies** — currencies you add yourself. They are visible only to
  you, and you set their exchange rate by hand.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

## In this section

- [Choosing which currencies you see](/docs/user-guide/currencies/#choosing-which-currencies-you-see)
- [Adding your own currency](/docs/user-guide/currencies/#adding-your-own-currency)
- [Editing or deleting a custom currency](/docs/user-guide/currencies/#editing-or-deleting-a-custom-currency)

---

## Choosing which currencies you see

A server can carry a long list of currencies, and you probably use two or
three. The switch next to each Econumo currency turns it on or off for your
account: only the currencies you keep enabled appear in the currency picker
when you [create an account](/docs/user-guide/accounts/#account-creation) or
budget. **Disable all** clears the list in one go, and the search field at the
top helps you find a currency in a long list.

**Note**
Your [default currency](/docs/user-guide/user-profile/#how-to-change-your-default-currency)
cannot be switched off — its toggle stays on and greyed out. Change the default
in your profile first if you want to retire that currency.

---

## Adding your own currency

Anything you count in units Econumo doesn't know about — loyalty points,
airline miles, a local voucher scheme, a cryptocurrency your server doesn't
carry — can become a currency of your own. Press **Create currency** and fill
in:

- **Name** — how the currency is labelled, e.g. "Points".
- **Code** — a short code, e.g. `PTS`.
- **Symbol** — what is shown next to amounts. Optional; the code is used when
  you leave it empty.
- **Decimal places** — the slider sets how many decimals amounts carry
  (2 by default; set it to 0 for something counted in whole units, like miles).
- **Exchange rate** — how many units of your currency one unit of your default
  currency is worth, entered as `1 USD = …`.

Your custom currency then behaves like any other: you can open an account in
it, and pick it for a budget or a single budget element. In the
screenshots throughout this guide, John's "Airline Miles" account uses a custom
**PTS** currency worth 10 to the dollar.

**Note**
A custom currency's rate is fixed — Econumo never updates it for you. If the
real rate moves and it matters to you, edit the currency to bring the number up
to date.

---

## Editing or deleting a custom currency

Open the three-dots menu next to a currency under **My currencies** and choose
**Edit** or **Delete**. Econumo currencies can only be switched on and off —
their details belong to the server, not to you.

---

# User Profile

URL: https://econumo.com/docs/user-guide/user-profile/

# User profile

This section provides an overview of user profiles in Econumo.

## In this section

  - [How to change your name](/docs/user-guide/user-profile/#how-to-change-your-name)
  - [How to change your email](/docs/user-guide/user-profile/#how-to-change-your-email)
  - [How to change your avatar](/docs/user-guide/user-profile/#how-to-change-your-avatar)
  - [How to change your password](/docs/user-guide/user-profile/#how-to-change-your-password)
  - [How to change your default currency](/docs/user-guide/user-profile/#how-to-change-your-default-currency)
  - [How to change the interface language](/docs/user-guide/user-profile/#how-to-change-the-interface-language)
  - [How to switch to dark mode](/docs/user-guide/user-profile/#how-to-switch-to-dark-mode)
