---
## Accessing your user profile

Open **Settings** and select the card with your name at the top of it — it is
labelled **Personal settings**, and so is the page it opens. The page shows
your personal details, preferences and security settings. To sign
out, press **Log out**: it sits under that card on the Settings page and at the
top of Personal settings.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

---
## Updating your user profile

### How to change your name

Type the new name in the "Name" field and tap outside it — the change is saved
automatically.

### How to change your email

Choose **Change email** in the Security section, enter your **New email** and
**Current password**, and press **Send confirmation code**. Econumo emails a
code to the new address to confirm you own it before the change takes effect;
your old address gets a notice, and every other session is signed out.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

### How to change your avatar

Click your avatar on the profile screen to open the avatar picker. Choose a
color and an icon, then press **Save**. Your avatar is shown to everyone you
[share](/docs/user-guide/shared-access/) accounts and budgets with.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

### How to change your password

Choose **Change password** in the Security section. Enter your current
password, then the new one twice:

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

**Note**
On a self-hosted instance with password sign-in turned off
(`ECONUMO_PASSWORD_LOGIN=false`), neither **Change password** nor **Set a
password** appears here — every sign-in goes through a linked provider
instead.

### How to change your default currency

The **Currency** preference in the Preferences section sets your default
currency in Econumo.

### How to change the interface language

The **Language** preference sits right below **Currency**. Open it and pick one
of the 11 available languages — English, Deutsch, Español, Français, Italiano,
Nederlands, Polski, Português, Русский, Українська, and 简体中文. The same
dialog is available from the language badge on the sign-in and sign-up screens,
before you have an account.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

### How to switch to dark mode

**Theme**, under **Language**, switches Econumo between **Light** and **Dark**.
**System** follows your device's appearance. The theme applies only to the
device you set it on.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

---
## Usage statistics and AI features

The last two Preferences each open a dialog with a single switch:

- **Usage statistics** → **Help improve Econumo**. Usage statistics show us
  which features are most popular and what to improve. Switching it off stops
  Econumo from sending in-app usage events right away, and the setting follows
  your account across devices.
- **AI features** → **Use AI features**. AI helps keep your finances organized
  — for example with [rule suggestions](/docs/user-guide/import-rules/#ai-rule-suggestions)
  for imported transactions. This preference appears only when your Econumo
  server has AI set up, and it is on by default. Turning it off stops
  everything that would send your data to the AI and removes your open
  suggestions.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

**Note**
Neither switch touches your budgets, transactions, or any other data in your
account. Your financial data and personal information, such as your name or
email, are never included in usage statistics and never sent to the AI.

---
## Sign-in methods

**Security → Sign-in methods** lists the external accounts you can use to sign
in instead of a password — Google, Apple, or a custom OpenID Connect provider,
whichever your Econumo instance enables. Each provider your instance turns on
appears here with a **LINK** button.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

Press **LINK** to connect a provider: Econumo hands you off to it to confirm
it's you, then brings you back with the provider listed as linked, its button
now reading **UNLINK**. From then on you can sign in either with your password
or with that provider.

**Note**
Unlinking is the same button in reverse. If a linked provider is the *only*
way into your account, Econumo won't let you remove the last one. For a
passwordless account, set a password first from **Change password**. On an
instance with password sign-in turned off, a stored password no longer counts
as a way in either, so the last remaining provider can't be unlinked at all —
the button is disabled with a note explaining why.

Linking or unlinking a provider emails you a notice, so gaining or losing a
way into your account never happens without you knowing.

---
## Sessions

**Security → Sessions** lists every device currently signed in to your account,
with the browser and operating system it was identified as and when it was last
active. Your current session is marked **Current**.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

Press **Revoke** next to a session to sign that device out, **Sign out** to end
the session you are using right now, or **Sign out other devices** to end every
session except the current one.

**Note**
If you spot a session you do not recognise, revoke it and
[change your password](/docs/user-guide/user-profile/#how-to-change-your-password).

---
## App lock

**Security → App lock** asks for a PIN or a pattern whenever Econumo opens on
this device — useful on a shared tablet or a phone you hand to your kids.

1. Switch on **App lock**.
2. Choose **PIN** (4 to 8 digits) or **Pattern** (connect at least 4 dots),
   enter it, and enter it again to confirm.
3. Under **Lock after**, choose when Econumo locks once you leave it:
   **Immediately**, after **1 minute**, **5 minutes** or **15 minutes**.

**Change PIN or pattern** asks for the current one first.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

**Note**
The lock protects Econumo on this device only, and it doesn't encrypt the data
stored on the device. If you forget the PIN or pattern, choose **Forgot PIN?**
(or **Forgot pattern?**) on the lock screen and log in again.

---
## API tokens

Econumo has a [REST API](/docs/api/), and personal access tokens are how you
authenticate against it — handy for scripts, home-automation dashboards, or any
integration of your own. Open **Security → API tokens** to manage them.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

Press **Create token**, give it a name that will remind you what it is for
(for example, "Home Assistant"), and choose when it expires: **30 days**,
**90 days**, **365 days**, a **custom date**, or **never**.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

**Note**
A personal access token grants full access to your account over the API — treat
it like a password. Create a separate token per integration so you can revoke
one without breaking the others.

The same tokens also authenticate Econumo's built-in MCP server. Claude and
Codex no longer need one — they sign in through the browser, see
[AI assistants (MCP)](/docs/user-guide/ai-assistants/) — but a token
still works for any MCP client that can't.

---
## Connected apps

**Security → Connected apps** shows the address of Econumo's built-in MCP
server — for Econumo, `https://app.econumo.com/mcp` — with a **Copy** button,
and lists every AI assistant you have allowed to use your account, with when it
was connected and when it was last used. **Revoke** signs an app out right
away.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

To connect Claude, Claude Code or Codex step by step, see
[AI assistants (MCP)](/docs/user-guide/ai-assistants/).

---

# AI assistants (MCP)

URL: https://econumo.com/docs/user-guide/ai-assistants/

# AI assistants (MCP)

Econumo has a built-in [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server. Connect
an AI assistant such as Claude, Claude Code or Codex to it, and the assistant
can check your balances and budgets, look up transactions, and log new ones for
you, straight from a chat.

You connect with your Econumo address only. You don't create or paste a token:
the assistant opens Econumo in your browser, you sign in, and you press
**Allow**.

## In this section

- [Your MCP address](/docs/user-guide/ai-assistants/#your-mcp-address)
- [Claude (web, desktop and mobile)](/docs/user-guide/ai-assistants/#claude-web-desktop-and-mobile)
- [Claude Code](/docs/user-guide/ai-assistants/#claude-code)
- [Codex](/docs/user-guide/ai-assistants/#codex)
- [Other MCP clients](/docs/user-guide/ai-assistants/#other-mcp-clients)
- [Managing connected apps](/docs/user-guide/ai-assistants/#managing-connected-apps)
- [Troubleshooting](/docs/user-guide/ai-assistants/#troubleshooting)

---
## Your MCP address

The address is your Econumo address followed by `/mcp`. For
[app.econumo.com](https://app.econumo.com) it is:

```text
https://app.econumo.com/mcp
```

You can also copy it in Econumo: open **Settings → Personal settings**, choose
**Connected apps** in the Security section, and press **Copy** next to the
address.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

**Note**
An app you allow can read and change all of your Econumo data. It never sees
your password, and its access works only for the MCP server, not for the rest
of the Econumo API.

---
## Claude (web, desktop and mobile)

1. In Claude, open **Settings → Connectors** and choose **Add custom
   connector**.
2. Paste your MCP address and add the connector.
3. Press **Connect**. Econumo opens in your browser. Sign in if you are asked
   to, check the app's name, and press **Allow**.

The connector then works in Claude on every device where you use the same
Claude account.

---
## Claude Code

Add the server from a terminal:

```sh
claude mcp add --transport http econumo https://app.econumo.com/mcp
```

Then start Claude Code, run `/mcp`, pick `econumo` and choose
**Authenticate**. Econumo opens in your browser. Sign in if you are asked to
and press **Allow**.

---
## Codex

```sh
codex mcp add econumo --url https://app.econumo.com/mcp
codex mcp login econumo
```

`codex mcp login` opens Econumo in your browser. Sign in if you are asked to
and press **Allow**. Flags can change between Codex releases;
`codex mcp add --help` shows the current ones.

---
## Other MCP clients

Any client that supports MCP's browser sign-in (OAuth) connects the same way:
give it your MCP address and allow it in Econumo.

A client that can't sign in through the browser can send a personal access
token instead. Create one in **Settings → Personal settings → API tokens** (see
[API tokens](/docs/user-guide/user-profile/#api-tokens)) and set the client to
send the header `Authorization: Bearer <your token>` to your MCP address.

---
## Managing connected apps

**Settings → Personal settings → Connected apps** lists every app you have allowed,
with when it was connected and when it was last used. **Revoke** signs an app
out right away; to use it again, connect it again.

A connection stays signed in while you use it. If an app is not used for 90
days, it asks you to sign in again.

Resetting your password through the emailed link disconnects every app.
Changing your password from Settings keeps them connected.

**Note**
On a self-hosted server, connecting by address needs `ECONUMO_URL` set to the
server's public **https** address, with no path (see
[Configuration](/docs/self-hosting/configuration/#ai-apps-mcp)). Without it,
Connected apps reads *"Connecting AI apps isn't available on this server"* and
the MCP server accepts [API tokens](/docs/user-guide/user-profile/#api-tokens)
only. Claude on the web, desktop and mobile connects from Anthropic's servers,
so for those the server must be reachable from the internet; Claude Code and
Codex only need to reach it from your computer.

---
## Troubleshooting

- **The client never opens a browser, or says the server doesn't support
  authorization.** Check the address ends in `/mcp` and has no typo. On a
  self-hosted server, check `ECONUMO_URL` as described above, and that a
  reverse proxy passes `/.well-known/*`, `/oauth/*` and `/mcp` through to
  Econumo, not only `/api`.
- **"This app sent an invalid request"** on the approval page. Go back to the
  app and start connecting again.
- **"This app's registration has expired or is unknown"** on the approval
  page. Make the app register again:
  - Claude: remove the Econumo connector and add it again.
  - Claude Code: run `/mcp`, pick `econumo`, choose **Clear authentication**,
    then **Authenticate**.
  - Codex: run `codex mcp logout econumo`, then `codex mcp login econumo`.
- **"This app is connected to a different Econumo account".** Someone else
  already connected this copy of the app. Add Econumo in your own Claude, Claude
  Code or Codex instead.
- **You can't press Allow.** A read-only account (for example, after a trial
  ends) can't connect an AI assistant.

---

# Import data

URL: https://econumo.com/docs/user-guide/import-data/

# Import data

Econumo was built around entering transactions by hand, and that still works
everywhere, with any bank. When you'd rather not type everything in, there are
three ways to bring transactions in, and you can mix them with manual entry
freely. All of them live in the **Data** group of **Settings**.

| | What it brings in | Good for |
|---|---|---|
| [CSV Import & Export](/docs/user-guide/csv-import-export/) | A file exported from your bank or another app | Your history, or a bank with no other connection; also exports your data |
| [Apple Wallet](/docs/user-guide/apple-wallet/) | Each Apple Pay purchase you tap to pay, as it happens | Card spending on an iPhone |
| [SimpleFIN](/docs/user-guide/simplefin/) | Your bank's transactions, each time you sync | Banks in the US and Canada, through the paid SimpleFIN Bridge service |

Transactions that arrive from Apple Wallet or SimpleFIN come with the bank's
text rather than your categories. [Import rules](/docs/user-guide/import-rules/)
classify them for you — or skip the ones you don't want — and with AI available
on your server, Econumo suggests rules as new imports come in.

Anything an import can't place on its own waits for you in the
[Inbox](/docs/user-guide/inbox/#imported-transactions).

---

# CSV Import & Export

URL: https://econumo.com/docs/user-guide/csv-import-export/

# CSV Import & Export

This section provides an overview of 'CSV Import & Export' in Econumo.

## In this section

- [Exporting your transactions to CSV](/docs/user-guide/csv-import-export/#exporting-your-transactions-to-csv)
- [Importing transactions from CSV](/docs/user-guide/csv-import-export/#importing-transactions-from-csv)

---
## Exporting your transactions to CSV

You can export your transactions to a CSV file for use in other applications
or for backup purposes.

To export your transactions:

1. Navigate to **Settings → Import & export**.
2. Click on **Export CSV**.
3. Select the account(s) you want to export transactions from.
4. Click **Export** to download the CSV file.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

---
## Importing transactions from CSV

Econumo allows you to import transactions from a CSV file. This is useful for
migrating data from other financial applications or for bulk adding
transactions.

CSV import requires the CSV file to be in a specific format. It must be
comma-separated values and include the following columns: Date, Amount, and
Account name. Optional columns are: Category, Description, Tags, and Payee
(Sender/Recipient).

The "Amount" column should contain positive values for income and negative
values for expenses. Alternatively, you can choose to import data from two
columns, "Inflow" and "Outflow," instead of "Amount".

To import transactions from a CSV file:

1. Navigate to **Settings → Import & export**.
2. Click on **Import CSV**.
3. Choose the CSV file you want to import (up to 10 MB).
4. Map the CSV columns to the corresponding fields in Econumo — the required
   fields (Account, Date, Amount) are marked with an asterisk.
5. Click **Import** to add the transactions to your account.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

**Note**
Example CSV format:
```csv
account_name,category,description,tag,payee,amount,spent_at
"Credit Card",Groceries,,,Costco,-500,"2026-01-04 13:01:32"
"Credit Card",Gas,,,Chevron,-50,"2026-01-04 13:01:51"
"Credit Card",Gifts,,,Costco,-100,"2026-01-04 13:03:51"
"Credit Card","Car Service",,car,,-150,"2026-01-04 13:04:51"
Cash,,,,,500,"2026-01-04 12:59:09"
Cash,Salary,,,,5000,"2026-01-04 13:02:17"
Cash,,"Transfer of 1000 USD to Savings",,,-1000,"2026-01-04 13:04:07"
Savings,,"Transfer of 1000 USD from Cash",,,1000,"2026-01-04 13:04:07"
Savings,,,,,20000,"2026-01-04 13:01:01"
```

---

# Apple Wallet

URL: https://econumo.com/docs/user-guide/apple-wallet/

# Apple Wallet

Connect Apple Wallet to Econumo to record purchases when you tap your iPhone
to pay with Apple Pay. An iPhone Shortcut sends the card name, merchant,
amount, and currency directly to Econumo.

## In this section

- [Before you start](#before-you-start)
- [Set up on iOS 26 or iOS 27](#setup)
  - [1. Install the Shortcut](#1-install-the-shortcut)
  - [2. Connect the Shortcut](#2-connect-the-shortcut)
  - [3. Create the automation](#3-create-the-automation)
    - [iOS 26](#ios-26)
    - [iOS 27](#ios-27)
  - [4. Make the first payment](#4-make-the-first-payment)
  - [5. Switch the automation to Run Immediately](#5-switch-the-automation-to-run-immediately)
- [Map your cards to accounts](#map-your-cards-to-accounts)
- [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)

## Before you start

You will need an iPhone running **iOS 26 or iOS 27**, Apple Pay set up with a payment
card, and the **Shortcuts** app, which comes with iOS. Allow about five minutes
for setup; the first payment needs to happen at a payment terminal.

Open Econumo on your iPhone and go to **Settings → Apple Wallet**. Tap
**Set up Apple Wallet** to open the five-step checklist. Keep it available
so you can return to it as you switch between Econumo and Shortcuts.

This integration works when you **tap your iPhone to pay**. Apple Pay
payments on websites aren't supported.

<div className="wallet-guide-screenshots">

</div>

---

## Setup

The five setup steps are the same on both versions. The redesigned Shortcuts
app on iOS 27 changes how you create the automation in **step 3** and enable
automatic runs in **step 5**; follow the instructions for your iOS version
in those steps. Screenshots for the shared steps were taken on iOS 26.

Keep confirmation enabled until the first payment has reached Econumo and
you have granted the requested permissions: **Run After Confirmation** on
iOS 26, or **Confirm Before Run** on iOS 27.

### 1. Install the Shortcut

In Econumo's setup checklist, open the **econumo** Shortcut link under
**Install the Shortcut**. In Shortcuts, tap **Add Shortcut**. The yellow
**econumo** tile will appear in your library.

Return to Econumo and tap **Done** under step 1.

<div className="wallet-guide-screenshots">

</div>

### 2. Connect the Shortcut

Tap **Connect the Shortcut** in Econumo. This creates an API token and opens
the Shortcut, which saves your Econumo server address and token.

When iOS asks whether **econumo** can send data to your Econumo server,
choose **Always Allow**. Use **Always Allow** for each data-access prompt
that offers it, so future payments can be sent without asking again. If
Shortcuts asks to display notifications, tap **Allow**.

Wait for the **Econumo configured** notification, then return to Econumo.
The checklist advances once the Shortcut has reached your server.

<div className="wallet-guide-screenshots">

</div>

### 3. Create the automation

#### iOS 26

1. Open **Shortcuts** and select the **Automation** tab.
2. Tap **New Automation**, or **+** if you already have automations.
3. Find and select **Wallet**.

<div className="wallet-guide-screenshots">

</div>

4. Select the payment cards and purchase categories you want to import.
   Select every category if you want all purchases from those cards. Leave
   **Filter Merchants** unset unless you want to limit which merchants trigger
   the automation.
5. Select **Run After Confirmation**, then tap **Next**.
6. Under **My Shortcuts**, select **econumo**. The automation now appears
   in the Automation tab.

Return to Econumo and tap **Done** under step 3.

<div className="wallet-guide-screenshots">

</div>

#### iOS 27

1. Open **Shortcuts**. If you are in **All Shortcuts**, tap the back arrow
   to return to **Library**.
2. Select **Automation** in Library.
3. Tap **+** at the bottom to create an automation.

<div className="wallet-guide-screenshots">

</div>

4. On the **New Shortcut** screen, tap **Edit** in the top-right corner.
5. Tap the **Search** field at the bottom and search for **Wallet**.
6. Choose **Wallet** under **Automation**, with the description
   **When I tap a Wallet Card or Pass**.

<div className="wallet-guide-screenshots">

</div>

7. Tap **Any Card** to choose the cards to import, or leave it as **Any Card**
   to include all cards. Leave **Categories** and **Merchants** as
   **Any Category** and **Any Merchant** to include all purchases from those
   cards. Keep **Automation**, **Notify**, and **Confirm Before Run** on
   for the first payment.
8. Search for **Run Shortcut** and add that action.
9. In the new action, tap the blue **Shortcut** placeholder and choose
   **econumo**.

<div className="wallet-guide-screenshots">

</div>

10. Expand the **Run econumo** action using its blue arrow if needed.
    Tap **Choose Variable** beside **Input** and select **Transaction**.
11. Check that the action reads **Run econumo** with **Input: Transaction**,
    then tap the back arrow. The new automation appears in the Automation
    list with its switch on.

Set the input to **Transaction** so Econumo receives the Wallet payment
details when the automation runs.

<div className="wallet-guide-screenshots">

</div>

Return to Econumo and tap **Done** under step 3.

### 4. Make the first payment

Make a purchase by tapping your iPhone to pay with one of the cards you
selected. When the automation asks, tap **Run**.

The first payment may bring up additional permission prompts. Choose
**Always Allow** on every prompt that offers it, including permission to
send the transaction to your Econumo server.

Return to Econumo and wait for the payment to arrive. Step 4 completes
automatically when Econumo receives it. The card will also appear under
**Cards**, where you can [map it to an account](#map-your-cards-to-accounts).

### 5. Switch the automation to Run Immediately

After the first payment has reached Econumo:

#### On iOS 26

1. Open **Shortcuts → Automation** and tap your Wallet automation.
2. Tap **Run After Confirmation** beside **Automation** at the top.
3. Choose **Run Immediately**.
4. Leave **Notify When Run** off if you don't want a notification each time
   the automation runs, then tap **Done** to save.

<div className="wallet-guide-screenshots">

</div>

#### On iOS 27

1. Open **Shortcuts → Library → Automation** and open the Wallet automation
   you created. It may be named **Run Shortcut**.
2. Turn off **Confirm Before Run** if it is shown, then turn off **Notify**.
   Keep **Automation** on. The final settings should look like the screenshot
   below, with **Automation** on and **Notify** off.
3. Tap the back arrow to return to the Automation list.

<div className="wallet-guide-screenshots">

</div>

Return to Econumo and tap **Done** under step 5 to finish the checklist.
This completes **Switch the automation to Run Immediately** in Econumo's
checklist on either version of iOS.

Future payments that match your selected cards, categories, and merchant
filters will be sent to Econumo without a confirmation prompt.

---

## Map your cards to accounts

In **Econumo → Settings → Apple Wallet**, find the card under **Cards**.
Choose **Map**, select the Econumo [account](/docs/user-guide/accounts/)
that represents that card, and confirm. Payments waiting for that card can
then be imported into the account, along with future payments.

Each newly used card needs its own mapping. Cards with the same name in
Wallet appear as one card in Econumo. Choose **Ignore** for a card you don't
want to import, or **Remap** to change its destination account later.

## Troubleshooting

- **The first payment hasn't arrived:** check that the automation uses the
  **econumo** Shortcut, includes the card and category you paid with, and
  doesn't exclude the merchant. While confirmation is enabled, you must
  tap **Run** after paying and grant the requested permissions. On iOS 27,
  also check that **Run econumo** has **Transaction** selected as its input.
- **The card appears, but the payment isn't in an account:** map the card to
  an Econumo account under **Settings → Apple Wallet**.
- **Every payment still asks for confirmation:** complete step 5 and save
  the automation with **Run Immediately** selected on iOS 26, or confirmation
  disabled on iOS 27.
- **You need to connect the Shortcut again:** use **Configure again** in
  Econumo's setup guide and follow the checklist. Connecting again replaces
  the token; open the Shortcut from the new connection link before expecting
  further imports.

For more about the Wallet trigger, see Apple's
[Shortcuts User Guide for iOS 26](https://support.apple.com/en-mide/guide/shortcuts/apd65c67538a/9.0/ios/26).
For the redesigned Shortcuts app, see
[Add automations on iOS 27](https://support.apple.com/en-mide/guide/shortcuts/apdfbdbd7123/10.0/ios/27).

---

# SimpleFIN

URL: https://econumo.com/docs/user-guide/simplefin/

# SimpleFIN

[SimpleFIN Bridge](https://bridge.simplefin.org/) is a paid third-party
service that connects to your bank — mostly banks in the US and Canada. Once
you connect it, Econumo pulls your bank transactions from it each time you
sync, so you don't have to type them in.

**Note**
Econumo is not affiliated with SimpleFIN. SimpleFIN Bridge has its own terms,
and you use it at your own risk.

## In this section

- [Connecting SimpleFIN](/docs/user-guide/simplefin/#connecting-simplefin)
- [Mapping bank accounts](/docs/user-guide/simplefin/#mapping-bank-accounts)
- [Syncing](/docs/user-guide/simplefin/#syncing)
- [Using SimpleFIN on another device](/docs/user-guide/simplefin/#using-simplefin-on-another-device)
- [Disconnecting](/docs/user-guide/simplefin/#disconnecting)

---

## Connecting SimpleFIN

1. In SimpleFIN Bridge, create a **New connection** and copy its **setup
   token**. A token can be used only once.
2. In Econumo, open **Settings → SimpleFIN** and paste the token into
   **Setup token**.
3. Choose a **Passphrase** (at least 8 characters) and type it again under
   **Repeat passphrase**.
4. Press **Connect**.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

Your SimpleFIN credentials are encrypted on your device with the passphrase,
and the server only ever stores them encrypted.

**The passphrase can't be recovered.** Nobody, including us, can restore it. If
you forget it, reconnect with a new setup token and a new passphrase — your
account mappings are kept.

SimpleFIN needs Econumo to be opened over **https** (or on `localhost`), because
the browser only encrypts the credentials on a secure page. On a self-hosted
server without https, ask your administrator to set it up.

The [Getting started](/docs/user-guide/#getting-started) wizard links here
from its **Connect** step, too.

---

## Mapping bank accounts

Once you connect, the page lists the bank accounts SimpleFIN reports under
**Needs mapping**. After a sync, each one shows how many transactions wait for
you (*"57 to review"*); they also wait in the
[Inbox](/docs/user-guide/inbox/#imported-transactions).

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

For each bank account:

- **Map** — pick the Econumo account its transactions go to, then press
  **Map**. The waiting transactions are imported right away.
- **Ignore** — for a bank account you don't want in Econumo. It moves to
  **Accounts** as *Ignored*, and you can still **Map** it later.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

A mapped account can be **Remap**ped to another Econumo account or **Unmap**ped.
After unmapping, its new transactions wait for review until you map it again.

When an imported transaction matches one you already entered by hand — a
transfer between your own accounts, say — Econumo matches the two instead of
adding a duplicate.

---

## Syncing

Press **Sync now** on the SimpleFIN page, or the sync button at the bottom of
the sidebar. The page shows when you last synced and from which date
transactions are fetched (*"Syncs transactions since …"*); press **Change** to
fetch from an earlier or later date.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

Imported transactions are classified by your
[import rules](/docs/user-guide/import-rules/). Anything Econumo can't place —
a bank account that isn't mapped yet, a currency without an exchange rate —
waits in the [Inbox](/docs/user-guide/inbox/#imported-transactions).

**Import history** lists every sync with what it imported, matched, updated,
queued or skipped. Open a run to see its transactions; one you deleted by
mistake can be imported again from there.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

---

## Using SimpleFIN on another device

On a device where you haven't used SimpleFIN yet, the page asks for your
passphrase — enter it and press **Unlock**. If you changed the passphrase on
another device, the page asks for the new one.

---

## Disconnecting

Press **Disconnect SimpleFIN** and confirm. The connection is removed from
Econumo; transactions imported earlier stay where they are.

---

# Import rules

URL: https://econumo.com/docs/user-guide/import-rules/

# Import rules

Transactions that arrive on their own — from [Apple Wallet](/docs/user-guide/apple-wallet/)
or [SimpleFIN](/docs/user-guide/simplefin/) — come with the bank's text, not
your categories. Import rules close that gap: a rule looks for some text in an
imported transaction and then classifies it, or skips it.

Rules apply only to imported transactions. Transactions you enter yourself are
never touched.

## In this section

- [Creating a rule](/docs/user-guide/import-rules/#creating-a-rule)
- [Rules from your corrections](/docs/user-guide/import-rules/#rules-from-your-corrections)
- [AI rule suggestions](/docs/user-guide/import-rules/#ai-rule-suggestions)
- [Ordering, editing and deleting rules](/docs/user-guide/import-rules/#ordering-editing-and-deleting-rules)

---

## Creating a rule

Open **Settings → Import rules** and press **Add rule**.

<ScreenshotSet>

</ScreenshotSet>

1. Under **When**, choose what to look at — the **Payee** or the
   **Description** the bank sent — and how to compare: **contains**, **starts
   with** or **is exactly**. Type the text to look for, for example
   _STARBUCKS_. The **Aa** button makes the match case-sensitive.
2. Under **Then**, choose what happens:
   - **Classify** — set a **Category** (pick **Expense** or **Income**: only
     transactions of that type get it), a **Payee**, and tags — a budget tag
     and any reporting tags.
   - **Skip** — matching transactions are not imported at all.
3. Press **Save**.

---

## Rules from your corrections

You don't have to write every rule by hand. When you change the category,
payee, tag or reporting tags of an imported transaction, Econumo offers to
**Create an import rule** for similar imports, with the match text filled in.
It can also apply the new rule to the other imported transactions it would
change.

---

## AI rule suggestions

When AI is available on your Econumo server, new imported transactions that no
rule classified get **rule suggestions** in your [Inbox](/docs/user-guide/inbox/#imported-transactions)
— one per merchant, for example *"BLUE BOTTLE · 3 transactions → Coffee · Blue
Bottle"*. Tap a suggestion to open the rule editor with the match text,
category and payee filled in. Saving creates the rule and fills in only the
**empty** fields of those transactions. **Dismiss** removes the suggestion.

The AI only picks from your existing categories and payees, and it never
changes a transaction by itself. On a shared account, suggestions go to the
account's owner.

To turn AI features off, open **Personal settings → AI features** — see
[User profile](/docs/user-guide/user-profile/#usage-statistics-and-ai-features).

---

## Ordering, editing and deleting rules

Rules run from top to bottom; drag a rule to change the order. Each rule's menu has **Edit** and **Delete**.

---

# Econumo apps

URL: https://econumo.com/docs/apps/

# Econumo apps

Econumo is a web application, but you can also use it as a regular mobile application on your iPhone, Android device, Mac, or PC.

---
## On iPhone:

1. Open the website [https://app.econumo.com](https://app.econumo.com) in Safari.
2. Tap the Share button (square with an upward arrow).
3. Select `Add to Home Screen` from the menu.
4. Rename the shortcut if desired, then tap `Add`. The web app will appear on your home screen and open in its own instance.

---
## On Android:

1. Open the website [https://app.econumo.com](https://app.econumo.com) in Google Chrome.
2. Tap the three-dot menu in the top-right corner.
3. Select `Add to Home Screen` or `Install App` (if available).
4. Confirm by tapping `Add`. The web app will now appear on your home screen and function like an app.

---
## On Mac

1. Open the website [https://app.econumo.com](https://app.econumo.com) in Safari.
2. Click `File > Add to Dock` from the menu bar, or click the share icon in the Safari toolbar and select `Add to Dock`.
3. Confirm by clicking `Add`. The web app will appear in your Dock, Applications folder, and Launchpad for easy access.

---
## On PC

1. Open the website [https://app.econumo.com](https://app.econumo.com) in Microsoft Edge.
2. Click the three-dot menu in the top-right corner.
3. Go to `Apps > Install this site as an app`.  
4. Confirm by clicking `Install`. The web app will be added to your Start menu and can also be pinned to your taskbar or desktop.
